---
title: "Research data access"
description: "How researchers can request access to restricted, de-identified BNR data."
---

BNR publishes aggregate data openly where this can be done safely. Some research questions require more detailed, restricted data. Access to those data is considered through a separate application and governance process.

## What can be requested

A request should identify:

- the research purpose and expected public health value;
- the disease area, population and period required;
- the minimum variables and detail needed;
- the proposed analytical outputs;
- ethics approval, where applicable; and
- secure storage, access and destruction arrangements.

## How decisions are made

Approval is not automatic. BNR considers the purpose, proportionality, sensitivity, disclosure risk, safeguards, legal and ethical position, and the feasibility of preparing a suitable dataset.

The principle of **data minimisation** applies: an approved dataset should contain no more detail than the project needs.

## Conditions of access

Approved users may be required to:

- sign the BNR Research Data Sharing Agreement;
- use data only for the approved purpose;
- restrict access to named team members;
- store data in the approved environment;
- submit proposed outputs for disclosure review; and
- return or securely destroy data at the agreed end point.

::: {.callout-important title="De-identified does not mean public"}
Detailed records can retain disclosure risk even when direct identifiers are removed. Restricted data must not be shared onward or placed in public repositories.
:::

## Start an application

[Open the Research Data Sharing Agreement](dsa-methods.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The agreement page explains how to complete, save and submit the document. The Info-Hub does not store information entered into the form.
